profile.name: Kamran Alam
profile.title: Full Stack Developer · Backend Focused
profile.tagline: I build REST APIs with Node.js, TypeScript and SQL databases, and the React apps that use them.
about: I'm a backend-focused Full Stack Developer with about a year of hands-on work: a paid freelance project and my current role at Viva Organization, where I joined as an intern and was promoted.
At Viva I work on a multi-tenant GST billing ERP in Node.js, Express and MySQL. I built its super-admin module: tenant provisioning, subscription plans, approval workflows and usage tracking.
My main side project is RooMates, an expense-splitting app where access control is enforced in PostgreSQL itself with Row-Level Security, and every change runs through tests in CI.
B.Tech in Computer Science from Galgotias University (CGPA 7.93). 200+ DSA problems solved on LeetCode and GeeksforGeeks.

points: Built the super-admin (platform control) module of a multi-tenant GST billing ERP: 40+ REST APIs for client and user management, tenant provisioning and subscription plans.
Built plan-upgrade and POS-access approval workflows (approve, reject, revoke). A request is marked approved only after tenant provisioning succeeds.
Added per-client usage tracking (growing, steady, declining, dormant) and invoice-limit middleware that counts by creation time, so backdating invoices can't bypass the monthly cap.
Worked on the database-per-tenant setup: tenant database provisioning, per-tenant schema migrations, status-change audit logs and session visibility.
Wrote 30+ Jest unit tests for provisioning, approvals, invoice limits, usage classification and super-admin access control.
Deploy and maintain applications on Linux servers (cPanel/WHM and VPS).
Built a School Management System for a school as a MERN app, first hosted on Vercel and Render.
Repackaged it as an Electron desktop app, installed it on the school's computers and handed it over.

projects.title: RooMates
projects.subtitle: Expense splitting and room listings
projects.description: Split rent and bills with roommates, settle up in the fewest payments, and find a room or flatmate. The focus is on the parts that are easy to get wrong: data privacy, money and abuse protection.
highlights: Room data stays private: PostgreSQL Row-Level Security and a least-privilege database role, on top of JWT with refresh-token rotation and Google sign-in
Money stored as integer paise and changed only through transactions, triggers and constraints
Debt-simplification algorithm settles any group in at most n-1 payments
Live updates with PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY pushed to open rooms over WebSocket
100+ automated tests on a real PostgreSQL, run by GitHub Actions on every push

highlights: REST API for income, expenses, categories and reports
Charts with Recharts, data in MongoDB Atlas
